normal_storyboard.title: Protein translation: initiation, elongation, and termination

scenes.description: Show an E. coli mRNA with 5' and 3' labels, a highlighted Shine-Dalgarno sequence upstream of AUG, and separate 30S and 50S subunits.
scientific_points: mRNA is read 5' to 3'.
Shine-Dalgarno sequence is upstream of the first AUG in E. coli.
Small subunit binds mRNA; large subunit binds tRNAs.
scenes.simplification_note: Bacterial example; eukaryotic initiation is not shown in detail.

scenes.description: Initiation complex forms: 30S binds mRNA; Shine-Dalgarno base-pairs with rRNA; initiation factors and GTP shown generically; fMet-tRNA enters P site directly; 50S joins to form intact ribosome with A, P, E sites.
scientific_points: Initiator tRNA enters P site directly, leaving A site free.
Intact ribosome forms after large subunit joins.
E. coli uses fMet-tRNA and Shine-Dalgarno anchoring.
scenes.simplification_note: Eukaryotic Met-tRNAi and 80S ribosome mentioned in caption, but detailed eIF/scanning omitted.

scenes.description: First elongation: a charged tRNA enters the free A site; its anticodon pairs with the mRNA codon after AUG.
scientific_points: Charged tRNA enters A site.
Anticodon-codon complementary base pairing.
scenes.simplification_note: Elongation factors and GTP hydrolysis shown only as energetic context, not molecular detail.

scenes.description: Peptide bond formation: peptidyl transferase in 50S catalyzes bond between A-site amino acid and P-site amino acid; growing polypeptide remains linked to P-site tRNA until translocation.
scientific_points: Peptidyl transferase is an RNA-based ribozyme in the large subunit.
Polypeptide remains linked to P-site tRNA until translocation.
scenes.simplification_note: No kinetic rate constants beyond the cited 0.05 s per amino acid are shown.

scenes.description: Translocation: ribosome advances three bases in the 3' direction; tRNAs shift A to P and P to E; former P-site tRNA enters E site and is expelled.
scientific_points: Translocation moves ribosome by three bases in 3' direction.
Order: A-site entry, peptide bond, translocation, E-site exit.
scenes.simplification_note: Steps are compressed for clarity; GTP hydrolysis and elongation factor names omitted.

scenes.description: Elongation cycle repeats, extending polypeptide from N terminus to C terminus while mRNA is read 5' to 3'.
scientific_points: mRNA read 5' to 3'; polypeptide synthesized N to C terminus.
Multiple cycles add amino acids.
scenes.simplification_note: Rate shown qualitatively; only cited 0.05 s per amino acid may be mentioned.

scenes.description: Termination: stop codon enters A site; release factor recognizes it; polypeptide detaches from P-site tRNA and is released; small and large subunits dissociate.
scientific_points: Stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA have no complementary tRNA.
Release factors trigger polypeptide release and subunit dissociation.
scenes.simplification_note: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic release factors shown generically.

scenes.description: Context panel: polyribosome on one mRNA; in prokaryotes transcription and translation can occur concurrently; in eukaryotes they cannot because RNA processing and nuclear export are required.
scientific_points: Polyribosome: many ribosomes translate one mRNA in same direction.
Prokaryotic transcription-translation coupling is possible; eukaryotic is not.
scenes.simplification_note: Selenocysteine/pyrrolysine recoding mentioned only as text exception, not animated.

evidence.quote: During initiation complex formation, bacterial fMet−tRNA fMet or eukaryotic Met-tRNAi enters the P site directly without first entering the A site, providing a free A site ready to accept the tRNA corresponding to the first codon after the AUG.

In E. coli mRNA, a leader sequence upstream of the first AUG codon, called the Shine-Dalgarno sequence (also known as the ribosomal binding site AGGAGG), interacts through complementary base pairing with the rRNA molecules that compose the ribosome.

issues: Contains one deliberately altered scientific relationship: initiator tRNA shown entering A site first.
This violates C4 event_order and would mislead students about the free A site available for the first elongation tRNA.
Must not be used as an educational artifact; only as a negative test case.

evidence.quote: During initiation complex formation, bacterial fMet−tRNA fMet or eukaryotic Met-tRNAi enters the P site directly without first entering the A site, providing a free A site ready to accept the tRNA corresponding to the first codon after the AUG.

reference_events.exact_quote: In E. coli , this complex involves the small 30S ribosome, the mRNA template, three initiation factors that help the ribosome assemble correctly, guanosine triphosphate (GTP) that acts as an energy source, and a special initiator tRNA carrying N -formyl-methionine(fMet-tRNA fMet )
reference_events.description: E. coli initiation complex includes 30S subunit, mRNA, three initiation factors, GTP, and fMet-tRNA_fMet.

reference_events.exact_quote: This interaction anchors the 30S ribosomal subunit at the correct location on the mRNA template.
reference_events.description: Shine-Dalgarno base-pairing anchors the 30S subunit on mRNA.

reference_events.exact_quote: At this point, the 50S ribosomal subunit then binds to the initiation complex, forming an intact ribosome.
reference_events.description: 50S subunit joins the initiation complex to form an intact ribosome.

reference_events.exact_quote: During initiation complex formation, bacterial fMet−tRNA fMet or eukaryotic Met-tRNAi enters the P site directly without first entering the A site, providing a free A site ready to accept the tRNA corresponding to the first codon after the AUG.
reference_events.description: Initiator tRNA enters P site directly, leaving A site free.

reference_events.exact_quote: The anticodon is a three-nucleotide sequence that bonds with an mRNA codon through complementary base pairing.
reference_events.description: tRNA anticodon pairs with mRNA codon by complementary base pairing.

reference_events.exact_quote: During each translocation event, the charged tRNAs enter at the A site, then shift to the P site, and then finally to the E site for removal.
reference_events.description: Charged tRNAs enter A site, shift to P site, then E site for removal.

reference_events.exact_quote: Peptide bonds form between the amino group of the amino acid attached to the A-site tRNA and the carboxyl group of the amino acid attached to the P-site tRNA.
reference_events.description: Peptide bond forms between A-site amino acid amino group and P-site amino acid carboxyl group.

reference_events.exact_quote: Ribosomal movements, or steps, are induced by conformational changes that advance the ribosome by three bases in the 3’ direction.
reference_events.description: Ribosome advances by three bases in the 3' direction.

reference_events.exact_quote: Each mRNA molecule is simultaneously translated by many ribosomes, all synthesizing protein in the same direction: reading the mRNA from 5’ to 3’ and synthesizing the polypeptide from the N terminus to the C terminus.
reference_events.description: mRNA read 5' to 3'; polypeptide synthesized N terminus to C terminus.

reference_events.exact_quote: As the ribosome steps across the mRNA, the former P-site tRNA enters the E site, detaches from the amino acid, and is expelled.
reference_events.description: Former P-site tRNA enters E site, detaches, and is expelled.

reference_events.exact_quote: On aligning with the A site, these nonsense codons are recognized by release factors in prokaryotes and eukaryotes that result in the P-site amino acid detaching from its tRNA, releasing the newly made polypeptide.
reference_events.description: Stop codon in A site recognized by release factors; polypeptide released.

reference_events.exact_quote: The small and large ribosomal subunits dissociate from the mRNA and from each other; they are recruited almost immediately into another translation init iation complex.
